title: 2 Kings Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 8.

questions.question: Who did Elisha speak to about the coming famine?
options: The woman whose son he restored to life
questions.correctAnswer: The woman whose son he restored to life
questions.explanation: Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had restored to life about the famine (2 Kings 8:1).

questions.question: How long did the famine last according to Elisha's prophecy?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven years
questions.explanation: Elisha told the woman that the famine would come upon the land for seven years (2 Kings 8:1).

questions.question: Where did the woman and her household sojourn during the famine?
questions.correctAnswer: Land of the Philistines
questions.explanation: The woman went with her household and sojourned in the land of the Philistines for seven years (2 Kings 8:2).

questions.question: True or False: The woman stayed in the land of Israel during the entire famine.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The woman left the land of Israel and sojourned in the land of the Philistines for seven years during the famine (2 Kings 8:2).

questions.question: What did the woman do after the famine ended?
options: Cried to the king for her house and land
questions.correctAnswer: Cried to the king for her house and land
questions.explanation: At the end of seven years, the woman returned and cried to the king for her house and land (2 Kings 8:3).

questions.question: Who did the king ask to tell him about Elisha's great works?
questions.correctAnswer: Gehazi
questions.explanation: The king talked with Gehazi, the servant of Elisha, asking him to tell all the great things Elisha had done (2 Kings 8:4).

questions.question: True or False: Gehazi told the king about Elisha restoring a dead body to life.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Gehazi told the king about how Elisha restored a dead body to life (2 Kings 8:5).

questions.question: What did the king do after hearing the woman's story?
options: Appointed an officer to restore her property
Asked Elisha to come to the palace
questions.correctAnswer: Appointed an officer to restore her property
questions.explanation: The king appointed an officer to restore all that was hers and the fruits of the field since she left the land (2 Kings 8:6).

questions.question: Who was sick when Elisha came to Damascus?
questions.correctAnswer: Benhadad king of Syria
questions.explanation: Benhadad king of Syria was sick when Elisha came to Damascus (2 Kings 8:7).

questions.question: What did the king of Syria instruct Hazael to do when he sent him to Elisha?
options: Take a present and ask if he shall recover
questions.correctAnswer: Take a present and ask if he shall recover
questions.explanation: The king told Hazael to take a present, meet Elisha, and inquire if he would recover of his disease (2 Kings 8:8).

questions.question: How many camels' burden of presents did Hazael bring to Elisha?
questions.correctAnswer: Forty
questions.explanation: Hazael brought a present of every good thing of Damascus, forty camels' burden (2 Kings 8:9).

questions.question: True or False: Elisha told Hazael that Benhadad would certainly recover from his disease.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Elisha told Hazael that Benhadad might recover, but the LORD showed him that he would surely die (2 Kings 8:10).

questions.question: What did Elisha do when Hazael asked why he was weeping?
options: He said he knew the evil Hazael would do to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He said he knew the evil Hazael would do to Israel
questions.explanation: Elisha wept because he knew the evil Hazael would do to Israel (2 Kings 8:12).

questions.question: In 2 Kings 8, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Elisha tells the woman to go sojourn due to famine
The king sends Hazael to meet Elisha
The woman cries to the king for her land
Gehazi tells the king about Elisha's miracles
questions.correctAnswer: Elisha tells the woman to go sojourn due to famine
questions.explanation: Elisha first told the woman to go and sojourn because of the coming famine before any other events occurred (2 Kings 8:1).

questions.question: True or False: The woman received back all her property and the fruits of her fields after the famine.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The king restored all that was hers and the fruits of the field since the day she left the land (2 Kings 8:6).

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Why did Elisha tell the woman to go and sojourn wherever she could?
options: Because the king commanded her to leave
Because the LORD had called for a famine that would last seven years
Because her son was ill again
Because the Philistines attacked her land
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD had called for a famine that would last seven years
questions.explanation: Elisha instructed the woman to leave because the LORD had called for a famine to come upon the land for seven years, as stated in 2 Kings 8:1 and 8:2.

questions.question: How long did the woman and her household sojourn in the land of the Philistines?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven years
questions.explanation: The woman obeyed Elisha and sojourned in the land of the Philistines for seven years, fulfilling the duration of the famine as per 2 Kings 8:2.

questions.question: What did the woman do when she returned from the land of the Philistines after seven years?
options: She went to Elisha for advice
She cried unto the king for her house and land
questions.correctAnswer: She cried unto the king for her house and land
questions.explanation: After seven years, the woman returned and appealed to the king for the restoration of her house and land, as recorded in 2 Kings 8:3.

questions.question: What was Gehazi's role in the woman's appeal to the king?
options: He was the king's servant who recounted Elisha's miracles
He was the king’s advisor on land disputes
questions.correctAnswer: He was the king's servant who recounted Elisha's miracles
questions.explanation: Gehazi, servant of Elisha, told the king of the great things Elisha had done, including restoring the woman's son to life, which supported her appeal (2 Kings 8:4-5).

questions.question: What did the king command after hearing the woman's story?
options: To restore all that was hers including the fruits of the field
To send her back to the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: To restore all that was hers including the fruits of the field
questions.explanation: The king ordered that all her property and the fruits of the field since she left be restored to her, showing his justice and recognition of Elisha's power (2 Kings 8:6).

questions.question: What was the condition of Benhadad king of Syria when Elisha came to Damascus?
questions.correctAnswer: He was sick
questions.explanation: Benhadad was sick when Elisha arrived in Damascus, which initiated the events involving Hazael's visit (2 Kings 8:7).

questions.question: What did King Benhadad instruct Hazael to do when meeting Elisha?
options: To inquire of the LORD by Elisha whether he would recover from his disease
To ask Elisha for advice on war
questions.correctAnswer: To inquire of the LORD by Elisha whether he would recover from his disease
questions.explanation: Benhadad sent Hazael to ask Elisha if he would recover from his illness, showing reliance on the prophet's connection to God (2 Kings 8:8).

questions.question: How did Elisha respond to Hazael's question about Benhadad's recovery?
options: He said Benhadad would surely recover
He said Benhadad would not recover and would die
He said Benhadad would recover but later die
questions.correctAnswer: He said Benhadad would recover but later die
questions.explanation: Elisha told Hazael to say Benhadad would recover from the disease, but the LORD revealed to Elisha that he would surely die, indicating God's sovereignty over life and death (2 Kings 8:10).

questions.question: Why did Elisha weep when Hazael visited him?
options: Because he was sad for Benhadad’s illness
Because he foresaw the evil Hazael would do to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Because he foresaw the evil Hazael would do to Israel
questions.explanation: Elisha wept because he knew the great evil Hazael would bring upon Israel, including burning strongholds and killing young men and pregnant women (2 Kings 8:11-12).

questions.question: What was Hazael's reaction when Elisha predicted the evil he would do?
options: He denied he could do such a great thing
questions.correctAnswer: He denied he could do such a great thing
questions.explanation: Hazael questioned, 'Is thy servant a dog, that he should do this great thing?' showing disbelief or humility at the evil he would commit (2 Kings 8:13).

questions.question: What did Elisha reveal about Hazael’s future?
options: He would become king over Syria
He would be a servant forever
questions.correctAnswer: He would become king over Syria
questions.explanation: Elisha told Hazael that the LORD had shown him he would be king over Syria, indicating God's plan despite Hazael's denial (2 Kings 8:13).

questions.question: How did Hazael kill King Benhadad?
options: By smothering him with a thick cloth dipped in water
questions.correctAnswer: By smothering him with a thick cloth dipped in water
questions.explanation: Hazael killed Benhadad by taking a thick cloth, dipping it in water, and spreading it on his face, causing his death and allowing Hazael to reign (2 Kings 8:15).

questions.question: Who began to reign in the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel?
options: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah
questions.explanation: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat began to reign as king of Judah during the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, marking a significant political event (2 Kings 8:16).

questions.question: How did Jehoram, son of Jehoshaphat, behave during his reign according to 2 Kings 8?
options: He walked in the ways of David and did good
He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and did evil in the sight of the LORD
He was a just and righteous king
questions.correctAnswer: He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and did evil in the sight of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jehoram followed the sinful ways of the kings of Israel, influenced by his marriage to Ahab's daughter, and did evil according to 2 Kings 8:18.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 8:19 promise will happen despite Jehoram's evil deeds?
options: The LORD would not destroy Judah for David's sake
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD would not destroy Judah for David's sake
questions.explanation: Verse 19 states that despite Jehoram’s evil, God would not destroy Judah because of His promise to David to maintain a light to him and his descendants.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 8.

questions.question: Who did Joram go to war against alongside Ahaziah, and where did this battle take place?
options: Hazael king of Syria at Ramothgilead
Benhadad king of Syria at Damascus
Pharaoh king of Egypt at Megiddo
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Hazael king of Syria at Ramothgilead
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 8:28 states that Ahaziah went with Joram to war against Hazael king of Syria in Ramothgilead.

questions.question: What was the outcome of Edom's revolt against Judah during Joram's reign?
options: Edom revolted and remained independent to this day
Edom was defeated and brought back under Judah's control
Edom formed an alliance with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Edom revolted and remained independent to this day
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 8:22 states that Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah and remained so to this day.

questions.question: How old was Jehoram when he began to reign in Judah, and how long did he reign?
options: Thirty-two years old; reigned eight years
Twenty-two years old; reigned one year
Thirty-two years old; reigned twenty years
Forty years old; reigned ten years
questions.correctAnswer: Thirty-two years old; reigned eight years
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 8:17 states that Jehoram was 32 years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What was the relationship between Ahaziah and the house of Ahab?
options: He was the son-in-law of the house of Ahab
He was a distant relative unrelated to Ahab
He was an enemy of the house of Ahab
He was a servant in Ahab's court
questions.correctAnswer: He was the son-in-law of the house of Ahab
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 8:27 specifies that Ahaziah was the son-in-law of the house of Ahab and walked in their ways.

questions.question: Which city did King Joram go to for healing after being wounded by the Syrians?
questions.correctAnswer: Jezreel
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 8:29 states that Joram went back to Jezreel to be healed from wounds given by the Syrians.

questions.question: What significant event occurred in the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab's reign in Israel?
options: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat began to reign in Judah
The famine began in the land
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat began to reign in Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 8:16 notes that in the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat began to reign in Judah.

questions.question: What literary device is illustrated by the parallel description of Joram and Ahaziah's evil reigns connected to the house of Ahab?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Verses 8:18 and 8:27 both describe Joram and Ahaziah walking in the way of Ahab and doing evil, illustrating parallelism in the narrative structure.

questions.question: In 2 Kings 8, what does the Hebrew word translated as 'revolt' (used regarding Edom and Libnah) most closely mean in its original context?
options: To break away or rebel against authority
questions.correctAnswer: To break away or rebel against authority
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root מָרַד (marad), translated as 'revolt' in 2 Kings 8:22, means to rebel or break away from established rule or authority.

questions.question: Which king succeeded Joram after his death?
questions.correctAnswer: Ahaziah his son
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 8:24 states that after Joram died, Ahaziah his son reigned in his stead.

questions.question: What cross-biblical passage also deals with the theme of Edom's revolt against Judah as mentioned in 2 Kings 8?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Chronicles 21:8-10
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 21:8-10 parallels the account of Edom's revolt in 2 Kings 8:20-22, illustrating the historical continuity of these events.

questions.question: What was the significance of Ahaziah’s mother being Athaliah, daughter of Omri king of Israel, in the context of his reign?
options: It linked him to the house of Ahab and influenced his evil actions
It made him a legitimate king of Israel
It caused peace between Israel and Judah
It prevented him from going to war
questions.correctAnswer: It linked him to the house of Ahab and influenced his evil actions
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 8:26-27 shows that Ahaziah’s maternal lineage connected him to the house of Ahab, contributing to his evil conduct.

questions.question: True or False: Joram's military campaign against Edom was successful in permanently restoring Edom under Judah’s control.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 8:21-22 describe Joram's attack against Edom and the flight of Edomites, but the passage also states Edom revolted and remained independent to this day, showing the campaign did not secure lasting control.

questions.question: True or False: The events of 2 Kings 8 foreshadow the continued conflict between Israel and Syria seen later in the Old Testament.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The warfare described in 2 Kings 8:28-29 between Israel and Syria under Hazael foreshadows ongoing hostilities detailed in later books such as 1 Kings and Isaiah.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 8:24 fulfill the theme of royal succession seen throughout the books of Kings and Chronicles?
options: By recording that Joram was buried with his fathers and succeeded by his son Ahaziah
By describing a rebellion overthrowing the king
By narrating the exile of the royal family
By recording a peaceful transfer of power to a foreign ruler
questions.correctAnswer: By recording that Joram was buried with his fathers and succeeded by his son Ahaziah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 8:24 shows the typical royal succession pattern where kings are buried with their ancestors and succeeded by their sons, a recurring theme in Kings and Chronicles.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage explicitly connects with Elisha’s prophecy about Hazael’s future kingship as introduced earlier in chapter 8?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:32-33 describes Hazael's reign over Syria, fulfilling Elisha’s prophecy in 2 Kings 8:13 about him becoming king.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by Elisha's instruction to the woman to sojourn because of the coming famine?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Elisha's warning about the seven years of famine demonstrates God's providence in forewarning His people to preserve life (2 Kings 8:1).

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 8:10-13, what does Elisha's prophecy regarding Hazael reveal about God's knowledge of human evil and sovereignty?
options: God is unaware of future human actions
God permits evil but does not know its extent
God foreknows evil deeds and sovereignly ordains rulers
God punishes all rulers immediately for evil
questions.correctAnswer: God foreknows evil deeds and sovereignly ordains rulers
questions.explanation: Elisha wept because he knew the evil Hazael would do, yet declared God had shown him Hazael would be king, revealing God's foreknowledge and sovereign control over human history (2 Kings 8:10-13).

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the king restoring the woman's property and land after seven years, as narrated in 2 Kings 8:5-6?
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness and justice
questions.explanation: The restoration of the woman's property shows God's justice and faithfulness to His people, ensuring restitution and blessing after hardship (2 Kings 8:5-6).

questions.question: How does the revolt of Edom and Libnah during Jehoram's reign, recorded in 2 Kings 8:20-22, contribute to the biblical narrative of covenantal consequences for sin?
options: It shows the faithfulness of God despite Israel's sin
It illustrates the covenantal curses for disobedience
It indicates God's abandonment of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the covenantal curses for disobedience
questions.explanation: The revolts demonstrate consequences of Israel and Judah's failure to walk rightly with God, consistent with covenant curses for disobedience (2 Kings 8:20-22).

questions.question: Synthesis: What combined doctrinal insight about God's justice and mercy can be drawn from the woman's restoration (2 Kings 8:5-6) and God's promise not to destroy Judah for David's sake (2 Kings 8:19)?
options: God is merciful but ignores justice
God balances justice with mercy based on covenant promises
God's promises are conditional on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: God balances justice with mercy based on covenant promises
questions.explanation: The restoration shows God's justice, while sparing Judah for David’s sake reveals His merciful covenant faithfulness, together affirming His balanced justice and mercy (2 Kings 8:5-6, 19).

questions.question: What does Elisha's weeping over Hazael's future evil deeds (2 Kings 8:11-12) reveal about the prophetic office in relation to divine revelation and human sin?
options: Prophets rejoice at all divine plans
Prophets share in God's sorrow over sin
Prophets are indifferent to human actions
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets share in God's sorrow over sin
questions.explanation: Elisha's weeping shows that prophets participate emotionally in divine grief over sin, highlighting their role as God's messengers sensitive to human evil (2 Kings 8:11-12).

questions.question: How does the narrative about Joram's reign and his alliance through marriage to Ahab's house (2 Kings 8:16-18) demonstrate the theological theme of covenant unfaithfulness?
options: It signifies covenant faithfulness through alliances
It illustrates departure from God's law through idolatrous influences
It indicates God's approval of Israel-Judah unity
It shows political neutrality in spiritual matters
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates departure from God's law through idolatrous influences
questions.explanation: Joram's marriage to Ahab's daughter and walking in Ahab's ways shows covenant unfaithfulness and influence of idolatry, indicating spiritual decline (2 Kings 8:16-18).

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by His preservation of Judah for David's sake despite the evil of King Jehoram (2 Kings 8:19)?
questions.correctAnswer: Grace
questions.explanation: God's withholding destruction from Judah because of His promise to David reveals His grace—undeserved favor and faithfulness to covenant promises (2 Kings 8:19).

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 8:25-27, how is the sinfulness of Ahaziah connected to the broader theological narrative of idolatry and covenant unfaithfulness?
options: Ahaziah worshipped the true God faithfully
Ahaziah's sin was independent of his family ties
Ahaziah's evil reflects the influence of Ahab's idolatrous house
questions.correctAnswer: Ahaziah's evil reflects the influence of Ahab's idolatrous house
questions.explanation: Ahaziah's walk in the ways of Ahab's house and his identity as son-in-law indicate covenant unfaithfulness influenced by idolatry (2 Kings 8:25-27).

questions.question: How does the death of Benhadad and ascension of Hazael (2 Kings 8:14-15) illustrate the theological principle of God's sovereign control over political powers?
options: God allows human rebellion without consequence
God ordains rulers and their timing, even through human evil
Kings reign by chance and not divine will
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains rulers and their timing, even through human evil
questions.explanation: Elisha's prophecy and Hazael's rise confirm God's sovereignty over political leadership, ordaining kings even amidst evil acts (2 Kings 8:14-15).

questions.question: Synthesis: What does the combined account of Elisha's miracles restoring life (2 Kings 8:1-2, 5) and his prophecy about Hazael's reign (2 Kings 8:10-13) teach about God's power over life, death, and history?
options: God's power is limited to miracles but not history
God controls both individual life and the course of nations
questions.correctAnswer: God controls both individual life and the course of nations
questions.explanation: The miracle of restoring life and the prophecy of Hazael's rise reveal God's sovereign power over both personal life and historical events (2 Kings 8:1-2,5; 8:10-13).

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 8:7-9 reveal about the role of prophetic intercession and inquiry to God in times of crisis?
options: Prophets inquire of God for guidance and healing
Kings do not seek God’s counsel
God does not communicate through prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets inquire of God for guidance and healing
questions.explanation: Benhadad sending Hazael to inquire through Elisha shows prophets as mediators who seek God's direction in crises (2 Kings 8:7-9).

questions.question: How does the revolt of Edom and Libnah during Jehoram's reign (2 Kings 8:20-22) serve as a theological indictment of Judah's covenant unfaithfulness?
options: It signifies God's blessing on Judah
It reflects God's judgment for unfaithfulness
It is unrelated to the covenant
It shows God's abandonment without cause
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects God's judgment for unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: The revolts are a direct consequence of Judah's failure to uphold the covenant, evidencing divine judgment (2 Kings 8:20-22).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the prophecy about Hazael's evil actions (2 Kings 8:12-13) is merely human conjecture and not divine revelation. What does 2 Kings 8:10-13 actually teach about prophetic knowledge and divine sovereignty?
options: Elisha's prophecy demonstrates divine revelation of future events
questions.correctAnswer: Elisha's prophecy demonstrates divine revelation of future events
questions.explanation: Elisha’s detailed prophecy about Hazael’s future evil and kingship shows that prophetic knowledge is divinely revealed and not mere conjecture (2 Kings 8:10-13).

questions.question: Synthesis: How do the narratives of Jehoram's and Ahaziah's reigns (2 Kings 8:16-19 and 2 Kings 8:25-27) collectively illustrate the biblical doctrine of generational sin and covenantal consequences?
options: Each king was righteous and faithful
The sins of one generation affect subsequent generations
Generational sin has no biblical basis
Covenantal promises negate all consequences of sin
questions.correctAnswer: The sins of one generation affect subsequent generations
questions.explanation: Both kings walked in the evil ways of Ahab’s house, illustrating how covenant unfaithfulness and sin can span generations with ongoing consequences (2 Kings 8:16-19; 8:25-27).
